desc:
For every position i of nums, count how many elements of the whole array are strictly smaller than nums[i], and return these counts as an array in the original order.

For example, [8, 1, 2, 2, 3] gives [4, 0, 1, 1, 3].
hints: Comparing every pair is O(n<sup>2</sup>). The values are small, so many positions share the same answer.
Count how many times each value from 0 to 100 occurs.
The answer for value v is the number of elements with value 0..v-1: a prefix sum over the counts. Then each position is a lookup.
editorial: Build cnt[v] for all values 0..100. Turn it into a prefix array less[v] = cnt[0] + ... + cnt[v-1], which is exactly the number of elements strictly below v. The answer for nums[i] is less[nums[i]].

This costs O(n + R) with R = 101, instead of O(n<sup>2</sup>) for pairwise comparison or O(n log n) for sorting with binary search. It is the counting-sort idea without actually producing the sorted array.
